## Proof

**Notation.** Set
$$\beta:=\lambda_1+\lambda_2-a_{11},\qquad \delta:=\lambda_3+\lambda_4-a_{33},$$
$$s_1:=\beta-a_{22}=(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)-(a_{11}+a_{22}),\qquad s_2:=\delta-a_{44}=(\lambda_3+\lambda_4)-(a_{33}+a_{44}).$$

The trace condition $\lambda_5=\sum a_{ii}-\sum_{j=1}^4\lambda_j$ gives the key identity
$$s_1+s_2=a_{55}-\lambda_5.\tag{0}$$

**Rewriting the entries.** With $\alpha:=\lambda_1-a_{11}$, $\gamma:=\lambda_3-a_{33}$, the off-diagonal entries become
$$a_{21}=\alpha(\lambda_1-\beta),\quad a_{23}=1+\gamma(\lambda_3-\delta),\quad a_{43}=\gamma(\lambda_3-\delta),$$
$$a_{24}=a_{44}-\beta,\quad a_{42}=a_{22}-\beta,$$
$$a_{51}=s_1\,a_{21},\quad a_{52}=s_1(\beta-a_{55}),\quad a_{53}=s_1\,a_{23}+s_2\,a_{43},\quad a_{54}=s_1(\delta-\beta)+s_2(\delta-a_{55}).$$

The last four follow by direct expansion; e.g.
$$a_{52}=s_1\beta-s_1(a_{33}+a_{44}+a_{55}-\lambda_3-\lambda_4)-s_1s_2=s_1\bigl(\beta-a_{55}\bigr),$$
using $\lambda_3+\lambda_4-s_2=a_{33}+a_{44}$, and
$$a_{54}=s_1(\delta-\beta)+s_2\delta-s_2a_{55}=s_1(\delta-\beta)+s_2(\delta-a_{55}).$$

**Two quadratic identities.** Define
$$f(t):=(t-a_{11})(t-\beta)-a_{21},\qquad g(t):=(t-a_{33})(t-\delta)-a_{43}.$$
Both are monic quadratics. Using $a_{21}=(\lambda_1-a_{11})(a_{11}-\lambda_2)$:
$$f(\lambda_1)=(\lambda_1-a_{11})(\lambda_1-\beta)+(\lambda_1-a_{11})(a_{11}-\lambda_2)=(\lambda_1-a_{11})\bigl[(\lambda_1-\beta)+(a_{11}-\lambda_2)\bigr]=0,$$
$$f(\lambda_2)=(\lambda_2-a_{11})(\lambda_2-\beta)+(\lambda_1-a_{11})(a_{11}-\lambda_2)=(\lambda_1-a_{11})\bigl[(\lambda_2-a_{11})+(a_{11}-\lambda_2)\bigr]=0.$$
Hence $f(t)=(t-\lambda_1)(t-\lambda_2)$. Likewise $a_{43}=(\lambda_3-a_{33})(\lambda_3-\delta)$ gives $g(\lambda_3)=g(\lambda_4)=0$, so
$$g(t)=(t-\lambda_3)(t-\lambda_4).\tag{1}$$

**Row reduction of $A-\lambda I$.** Write the rows of $A-\lambda I$ as $R_1,\dots,R_5$. Perform the row operation (which preserves the determinant)
$$R_5\;\longleftarrow\;R_5-s_1R_2-s_2R_4.$$
Computing each component of the new $R_5$, using $a_{42}+s_1=0$, $a_{22}+s_1=\beta$, $a_{24}+s_2=\delta-\beta$, $a_{44}+s_2=\delta$, and (0):

- Col 1: $a_{51}-s_1a_{21}=0$.
- Col 2: $a_{52}-s_1(a_{22}-\lambda)-s_2a_{42}=s_1(\beta-a_{55}-a_{22}+\lambda)+s_2(\beta-a_{22})=s_1(s_1+s_2-a_{55}+\lambda)=s_1(\lambda-\lambda_5)$.
- Col 3: $a_{53}-s_1a_{23}-s_2a_{43}=0$.
- Col 4: $a_{54}-s_1a_{24}-s_2(a_{44}-\lambda)=s_1(\delta-a_{44})+s_2(\delta-a_{44}-a_{55}+\lambda)=s_2(s_1+s_2-a_{55}+\lambda)=s_2(\lambda-\lambda_5)$.
- Col 5: $(a_{55}-\lambda)-s_1-s_2=-(\lambda-\lambda_5)$.

So the new fifth row is $(\lambda-\lambda_5)\,[\,0,\;s_1,\;0,\;s_2,\;-1\,]$, and
$$\det(A-\lambda I)=(\lambda-\lambda_5)\,\det N(\lambda),$$
where $N(\lambda)$ has rows $R_1,R_2,R_3,R_4$ and last row $[\,0,s_1,0,s_2,-1\,]$.

**Eliminating column 5.** In $N$, perform $R_2\leftarrow R_2+R_5$ and $R_4\leftarrow R_4+R_5$ (row additions, determinant unchanged). Since $R_2$ and $R_4$ both have entry $1$ in column $5$ while $R_5$ has $-1$, column $5$ of the new $R_2,R_4$ vanishes. Using $a_{22}+s_1=\beta$, $a_{24}+s_2=\delta-\beta$, $a_{42}+s_1=0$, $a_{44}+s_2=\delta$:
$$N'=\begin{bmatrix}
a_{11}-\lambda & 1 & 0 & -1 & 0\\
a_{21} & \beta-\lambda & a_{23} & \delta-\beta & 0\\
0 & 0 & a_{33}-\lambda & 1 & 0\\
0 & 0 & a_{43} & \delta-\lambda & 0\\
0 & s_1 & 0 & s_2 & -1
\end{bmatrix}.$$

Expanding along column $5$ (only the $(5,5)$ entry $-1$ is nonzero):
$$\det N' = -\det\begin{bmatrix}
a_{11}-\lambda & 1 & 0 & -1\\
a_{21} & \beta-\lambda & a_{23} & \delta-\beta\\
0 & 0 & a_{33}-\lambda & 1\\
0 & 0 & a_{43} & \delta-\lambda
\end{bmatrix}.$$

**Block-triangular factorization.** The $4\times4$ matrix above is block lower-triangular (rows $3,4$ have zeros in columns $1,2$), so its determinant factors:
$$\det\begin{bmatrix}a_{11}-\lambda&1\\a_{21}&\beta-\lambda\end{bmatrix}\;\cdot\;\det\begin{bmatrix}a_{33}-\lambda&1\\a_{43}&\delta-\lambda\end{bmatrix}.$$
The first factor is $(\lambda-a_{11})(\lambda-\beta)-a_{21}=f(\lambda)=(\lambda-\lambda_1)(\lambda-\lambda_2)$. The second is $(\lambda-a_{33})(\lambda-\delta)-a_{43}=g(\lambda)=(\lambda-\lambda_3)(\lambda-\lambda_4)$, by (1).

Therefore
$$\det N'=-\,(\lambda-\lambda_1)(\lambda-\lambda_2)(\lambda-\lambda_3)(\lambda-\lambda_4),$$
and
$$\det(A-\lambda I)=(\lambda-\lambda_5)\,\det N=(\lambda-\lambda_5)\,\det N'=-(\lambda-\lambda_1)(\lambda-\lambda_2)(\lambda-\lambda_3)(\lambda-\lambda_4)(\lambda-\lambda_5).$$

Since $A$ is $5\times5$, $\det(A-\lambda I)=(-1)^5\prod_{i=1}^5(\lambda-\lambda_i)=-\prod_i(\lambda-\lambda_i)$, which is exactly what we obtained. Hence the characteristic polynomial of $A$ is $\prod_{i=1}^5(\lambda-\lambda_i)$, and the spectrum of $A$ is $\{\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3,\lambda_4,\lambda_5\}$. $\blacksquare$

$$a_{21}=\alpha(\lambda_1-\beta),\quad a_{23}=1+\gamma(\lambda_3-\delta),\quad a_{43}=\gamma(\lambda_3-\delta),$$

$$f(t):=(t-a_{11})(t-\beta)-a_{21},\qquad g(t):=(t-a_{33})(t-\delta)-a_{43}.$$
Both are monic quadratics. Using $a_{21}=(\lambda_1-a_{11})(a_{11}-\lambda_2)$:

Hence $f(t)=(t-\lambda_1)(t-\lambda_2)$. Likewise $a_{43}=(\lambda_3-a_{33})(\lambda_3-\delta)$ gives $g(\lambda_3)=g(\lambda_4)=0$, so

0 & 0 & a_{43} & \delta-\lambda & 0\\
0 & s_1 & 0 & s_2 & -1
\end{bmatrix}.$$

0 & 0 & a_{33}-\lambda & 1\\
0 & 0 & a_{43} & \delta-\lambda
\end{bmatrix}.$$

$$\det\begin{bmatrix}a_{11}-\lambda&1\\a_{21}&\beta-\lambda\end{bmatrix}\;\cdot\;\det\begin{bmatrix}a_{33}-\lambda&1\\a_{43}&\delta-\lambda\end{bmatrix}.$$
The first factor is $(\lambda-a_{11})(\lambda-\beta)-a_{21}=f(\lambda)=(\lambda-\lambda_1)(\lambda-\lambda_2)$. The second is $(\lambda-a_{33})(\lambda-\delta)-a_{43}=g(\lambda)=(\lambda-\lambda_3)(\lambda-\lambda_4)$, by (1).

$$\det N'=-\,(\lambda-\lambda_1)(\lambda-\lambda_2)(\lambda-\lambda_3)(\lambda-\lambda_4),$$
and

Since $A$ is $5\times5$, $\det(A-\lambda I)=(-1)^5\prod_{i=1}^5(\lambda-\lambda_i)=-\prod_i(\lambda-\lambda_i)$, which is exactly what we obtained. Hence the characteristic polynomial of $A$ is $\prod_{i=1}^5(\lambda-\lambda_i)$, and the spectrum of $A$ is $\{\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3,\lambda_4,\lambda_5\}$. $\blacksquare$
